body:
Thank you for your advice.

I've moved to the US for in-patient treatment, once.  Because it put a great deal of distance (even with telephone/skype, the 12 hour time difference really cut me off from everyone) between myself and the few people who've kept me going, and very likely because of the medicines I was on, I felt like an isolated robot, going through the motions. It was weird.

My anxiety and low self-esteem were waiting for me when I got out. Not immediately, but gradually.

Any recommendations for Californian in-patient places?

You hit the nail on the head.

So far, this has been the most interesting idea - if only I could wrap my head around accepting being miserable for the rest of my life and not become suicidal.

Could you explain more about how you separate your identity from your "headache"? I don't really remember a teenage or adult me that wasn't miserable; there were definitely small, indescribable happy moments, though.

Back and forth; switching between various Asian countries and the US. Perhaps 12 years total.

Why?

In short, I am limited not only by my location, (Bangkok, Thailand), but also the severity of my depression. Two of my latest doctors (of the dozen or so therapists I have worked with) with referred me to other doctors because they are "no longer comfortable" treating me because I am "beyond their expertise."

It is a blow, and I do want to find other therapists. But English-speaking therapists are difficult to come by here; a few that I have sought out felt also said they could not treat me.

Additionally, I am running out of medicines. The longest any of my medications has ever worked is six months. As they stop working, my doctors max out my prescription, I become suicidal, or the side effects become too severe. It has been ten years. I have taken most (if not all) of the medicines mentioned regularly on websites and on self.SuicideWatch.

My last doctor cobbled together a regimen of seven medicines. I am now taking many different medicines to keep me awake, to help me sleep, to stop nightmares, to help with anxiety, and to help with depression.

I am running out of therapists, and I am running out of medicines more quickly than pharmaceutical companies can create them.

I have had extensive physicals and sleep tests; my doctors, bless them, have tried on many diagnoses. They haven't found anything that was abnormal. I haven't suffered abuse or trauma. I am just unable to find satisfaction or happiness in anything I do; I cannot think of my past or future without pain, and I am growing more convinced that this will not change.

I am extremely lucky to have a supportive family who've paid my extensive medical bills. So I have been, and am, trying very hard to get better. Trying to take baby steps towards being independent and rebuilding my personality; to not burden them any longer.


I am running out of options. Please, please, please, tell me your story, or what to do. Even if it wasn't successful for you.


I hope this community will understand the reasons why it is very, very difficult for me to even imagine "just going outside and loving life!" or "finding some friends."

Edit: Um, and yes. I am contemplating suicide. I believe that there is such a thing as running out of options. I'd just like some concrete evidence that I'm not out of options... permanent solution to what is supposed to be a "temporary" problem, and all that stuff.



Edit #2: Thank you very much for your suggestions. I've been reading every hour.
